title: Three antipatterns on stage: overload, negation, and the rewritten contrast

events.label: The raw request
events.detail: "Help me process this product blurb." — one sentence, five implied expectations: rewrite, translate to English, add a title, bullet the selling points, keep it under 50 words.

events.label: Antipattern one: the overloaded instruction
events.detail: v1 stuffs five demands into one sentence: "Rewrite this blurb, translate it into English, add a title, list the selling points as bullets, keep it within 50 words…" — no separation between tasks.

events.label: v1 call
events.detail: The model's behavior on overloaded instructions: do the easy parts, quietly drop the rest.

events.label: v1 evaluation: two items dropped
events.detail: Rewrite, translation, and title done; the bullet list is missing and the body runs 112 words against a 50-word cap. Pack ten tasks into one sentence and the model will drop some — without telling you.

events.label: The fix: split and number
events.detail: v2 turns the five demands into a numbered list, one requirement per line, boundaries clean. Method: change only this one thing, keep v1 archived for comparison.

events.label: v2 call
events.detail: Everything else stays as close to unchanged as possible — the only variable in this controlled experiment is instruction structure.

events.label: v2 evaluation: 5/5
events.detail: All five requirements met, body at 48 words. Same model; the listing alone delivers an immediate lift.

events.label: Antipattern two: negative instruction
events.detail: A second contrast track: v1b tries to constrain style with "do not use passive voice in the reply" — negative phrasing is a classic trap.

events.label: v1b output: passive anyway
events.detail: The output duly contains "The features are loved by users…" — the attention weight on "do not X" is often too weak, and the model does exactly the forbidden thing.

events.label: The positive rewrite
events.detail: v3 flips the ban into a positive instruction: "write everything in active voice" — say what you want, not what you don't.

events.label: v3 evaluation: passes
events.detail: Active voice throughout. Positive instructions execute markedly more reliably than negative ones — not mysticism, just how attention prefers instructions.

events.label: Method wrap-up
events.detail: Three rules of prompt repair: change one thing at a time, keep before/after records, tie changes to effects. Also — polite padding and threats contribute nothing to capability; deleting them saves tokens. And "jailbreak-style stress testing" means nothing in production; for evaluation see G01.
